title: The Tallest Mountain on Earth Is Hiding

beats.narration: Mount Everest stands 8,849 metres above sea level — the highest point on Earth.
But height depends on where you start measuring. And Everest doesn't start from the bottom.
sources: Measurement convention: elevation above sea level (NOAA)

beats.narration: Measured from its base on the Pacific floor, Mauna Kea rises 10,210 metres — more than a kilometre taller than Everest.
sources: USGS: Mauna Kea base-to-peak 10,210 m; summit 4,207 m

beats.narration: It was built by a hotspot: eruptions stacked lava, layer upon layer, for around a million years.
sources: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory: Mauna Kea shield stage ~1 Ma

beats.narration: Most of the mountain hides underwater. Only 4,207 metres breaks the surface — about 41 percent.
sources: USGS/NOAA: 4,207 m above sea level; 6,003 m below (59%)

beats.narration: So Everest is the highest mountain. Mauna Kea is the tallest — and it spends most of its life in the dark.
